I have used many monitors over the years and this is by far the best one! The picture quality is amazing, it is very customizable and it has a super long battery life. I bought at a slightly more expensive price, but even for what I paid I am super happy with the purchase. The only issue I encountered was with the thermometer. It stopped working after a few says. However I went back to the email the company sent me when I first purchased this in order to contact them but there were instructions to update the software that I hadn’t read. It was a little annoying but didn’t take too long and that fixed the problem. I like that as they fix and update their product I don’t have to buy newer models and can update mine at home.

Things I love about this monitor
• Very clear picture
• Can use all over my house. This was something I worried about because we have a large brick fireplace in the center of our house and I wasn’t sure if that would interfere with Althea signal, but it didn’t.
• Super long battery life even with the screen on
• You can customize the brightness, sound and tons of other features. I like that I can turn off the night vision. Sometimes when it is just light enough the camera can’t tell the difference and keeps switching between normal and night vision and it can get annoying. But with this camera I can manually change it to normal vision.
•Easy to set up camera that has a huge visual field.

A few things I wished they would change
• There is no eco mode that switches on the sound and screen when there is loud noises heard. I like to turn down the sound because my daughter has a white noise machine and the constant hum is annoying to listen to. So instead I have to keep the screen on which can be distracting when you are trying to do other things. They do have a feature where you can set a certain noise level in which it will set off an alarm, but the alarm is obnoxiously loud and you can’t stop it until it beeps for the full ten seconds. If only you could set the noise level to turn on the sound and screen it would be perfect! It works for us because our daughter’s room is across the hall so I turn off the sound at night since we can hear her cry. But I wouldn’t want to wake up my husband every time I have to get up or vice versa.
•There is no alarm if you are out of range or the monitor is about to run out of batteries. These two are not deal breakers for me but just something to be aware of.

Overall the absolute best monitor out there! I did tons of research and have used many monitors in my career as a nanny and nothing has compared to this one!

Great camera with too many quality control issues-excellent customer service. Update 1/9/2020

Sorry I’ve gone back and forth but I’m done-it stopped working again and now my son relies on the music to help him sleep. It disconnected and no matter what cords we use or outlet we use, the monitor won’t connect to the camera. One star-great customer service but I shouldn’t have to deal with this.

Update 1/2/2020

Eufy has amazing customer service. They saw my review and urged me to try some new cables which they sent me free of charge. I was hesitant because I didn’t want the problem to occur later on, but since they had been so good to me, I decided to give the new cables a shot. I’ve been using the new cables for 2 months and the camera has not failed yet! I’m bumping my review back up to three stars. Further, for the trouble, eufy refunded me half of the price of the monitor.

All in all, for my troubles with this product over the past year, they’ve sent me three new systems, a new set of cables, refunded half the price of what I paid, a Bluetooth speaker for my troubles, and a charging pad for my phone. I didn’t ask to be compensated for any of this-they just offered without hesitation.

So their customer service is awesome-always willing to help and take suggestions for improving the device. The monitor, when it works, is better than any other on the market. I’ve tried several others and they are all cheap-the music on them sucks and sounds horrible out of the speakers, the screen is small, and it’s a pain to mount some of the cameras. Plus-you can’t apply software updates to the other ones I’ve tried.

However, I don’t think I should have to be the guinea pig for a product commercially available. There should be no need to send out three versions of a product. That makes it seem like there are some quality control issues.

So buy this product and know you’ll get great customer service, but you might have to use that customer service because there could be issues with the monitor.

Update: 11/17/19

I can no longer endorse this product. While there have been bugs and the company has been extremely helpful in fixing these bugs, there are just too many for this product to be available to the public-this past week was the final straw.

It seems there is a problem with where the USB cable connects to both the power plug and the monitor/camera itself. I went to bed, thinking the monitor was charging, and woke up to a dead monitor and my baby screaming in the other room. I figured it was user error at first, even though I’ve used this monitor for almost a year, so I tried it again the next day. With the monitor, when I wiggle the usb cord and the power plug, it loses power randomly. There’s some faulty connection there. I can’t have this, not with my baby in the other room and my reliance on this product working.

Similarly, there’s a weak connection with the camera. I traveled with this monitor two weeks ago and had to set it up at my parents house and on three occasions, the camera lost connectivity and the only solution was to wiggle the power cord until it got power back to it.

I’ll be buying something else and will reduce this to one star. There simply needs to be more testing done on this product.

Update: 8/31/19

The Eufy monitor continues to be really great and the customer support is amazing. However, the battery life has severely dropped over the last few weeks. We've had this for roughly 8-9 months and now we have to plug it in during the day when he is sleeping or else the battery will quickly die out. I think what hurts the battery life is when our son is trying to go to sleep, we have the video on for however long that takes with the music play, and so sometimes the video will be on with the music for up to 30 minutes at times. He takes 1-2 naps a day now at 10 months old and so the video/music may play for an hour a day and the battery just isn't up to the task for that. It's a shame because we love everything about the monitor, but it's a pain to keep the charger cable and the monitor plugged in wherever we go. It's not a issue at night because we plug it in, but if we're downstairs doing laundry or watching tv, it's a pain to run up and grab the charger. I wish the battery was replaceable in these. Still 5 stars because it's a great product, but the battery definitely hurts.

Update: 5/13/19

Eufy customer service e-mailed me yesterday to inform me of a software update which gives the option of turning the video screen ON when a certain audio level is reached (you can selected the noise level on a scale of 1-5 with 5 being the loudest) WITHOUT emitting an alarm. This is something that has been asked for by the community for quite some time. In the past, you could only turn the screen on with a VERY loud alarm which was annoying when we were sleeping. So this update is huge.

While I wish they would come out with a better way to get these updates out to the community (right now they just send me an e-mail through Amazon customer service informing me of the update...so if any user hasn't emailed them to inquire about their product, they are kinda stuck with it), this monitor now has everything I need in a baby monitor. Yes, the kickstand isn't as robust as some other products, but I don't mind it. I'm updating this review to 5 stars. I wouldn't consider buying anything else.

Update: 4/21/19

Eufy Customer service has been great. They immediately e-mailed me instructions on how to update the firmware and that helped the temperature a bit, but it was still about 3 degrees higher than what the ambient temperature in the room was. I e-mailed them again and their engineers went and sent another update to me. Life has gotten in the way recently with a newborn, but I finally downloaded the new firmware today and the temperature is reading EXACTLY what it should be with ZERO issues. For the inconvenience, Eufy also sent me a free bluetooth speaker, which was nice.

I've updated the review to 4 stars, from it's original 3 stars. The only reason this product doesn't have 5 stars are for these two reasons:

1) The kickstand sucks. As the wirecutter review noted, it's too easy for it to fall over. They should update the model with a new stand.
2) While customer service is great, they need to come out with a new way to update firmware for their products. Right now, they basically send me an e-mail to search for something like "e7fjCh5fk" in Youtube, and that gives me a link to a how-to video from their engineers on where to download some files and update their firmware. A company as large as this should really invest in a central website people can go to to view these files and download the updated firmware.

All in all, I would recommend purchasing this baby monitor-the video quality is second to none.

Update: 2/23/19

We received the new monitor and it seemed to work great for a day, and then the temperature was back up to 143 degrees for a few minutes before dropping down to 73 degrees. It switches intermittently it seems. I've e-mailed the company and hopefully they have a fix.

First, the charge cords are short. I mean very short. I couldn't even plug the cameras in to the wall plugs and hang them up high enough to see the whole room.
Second, I cannot figure out how to set these up. It seems like the cameras change their settings on their own. Plus they are constantly dropping from the monitor, and I was always well within the 600 ft range. And not to mention the monitor automatically divides in split screen into 4 sections. Meaning if you only have 2 cameras, you have empty, wasted screen space.
Third, the camera functions themselves. The first option is scan. This is where the cameras pan back and forth between the rooms. You can't hear sound from both rooms, which is understandable. But if the monitor is viewing room 2 and the baby is crying in room 1, you don't know for 12 seconds. Maybe not a big deal to some, but it means enough time for my son to get really worked up. So you remedy this by setting the cameras on split screen. But split screen has no sound at all, only a sound alert, which is basically a high pitched beep, and a box shows you which room the sound is coming from. Next time it didn't pick up the baby crying.
And the last problem I had was while set on scan mode, you can turn off the LCD screen, helpful for those that don't sleep with light. Well, mine kept turning itself back on. And back on. And back on. One night, when no one was making any noise, I set it back to 'off' 30 times.

The camera quality is really good, the night vision is really good and being able to move the camera from the screen is good and the good things end there.
Temperature sensor is OMG bad! It is consistently off 3-5 degrees the actual value! This sensor would show 74 and the actual temperature in the nursery would be 69 (measured by +/- 0.5F precision thermometer). We relied on this thermometer and dressed the baby accordingly and the baby would wake up all the time.
The battery of the screen is so bad, they claim 8-12 hours, we never really got over 4-5 hours. For something we use daily, throughout the day for naps, we would have loved it if it actually worked for as many hours as claimed.
The built in mic is useless, you say something into the mic and on the other side you would hear is imperceptible and broken. Tried using it twice and gave up!

Overall buy something cheaper if all you need is video. Buy something more expensive if you need all the features to be working as claimed by this monitor

Camera itself and Picture Quality are Good, App is Terrible. I got this monitor for my son's nursery because I wanted a video monitor that would allow me to check in on him wherever I was and that would notify me if he started to move or make noise. The camera itself I have no problems with - picture is clear and the night vision works well. That said, we have had MORE than a few issues with the app that connects to the camera - Notably:

1) When I first set it up, there were no clear instructions in the app on how to add/invite my husband on to the account. He went to set it up himself and ended up creating a second account which then kicked me off. We then went to the internet and found that all he would have had to do was log into the account that I created. This was, in the end not a big deal and pretty simple to solve but it would have been really helpful if the app had a way to invite your partner to the account once you've set it up or if there was a setup option to connect to an existing/functioning camera.

2) I use an iPhone, my husband has an Android - we've both found that the app has bugs - the most common issue for both of us that if I leave the app open on my phone (e.g. do not swipe and force close it) and then try to check in again after a few minutes it won't connect and I have to force close and restart anyway. Again, not a huge deal but annoying when my son is napping and I'm wanting to check on him regularly. My husband's Android version would also unmute the audio if he restarted - if he didn't force close the app, he would not see video but would hear audio even though he had previously turned it off.

3) Dream Lab - When my son turned 4 months, the app encouraged us to check out the Dream Lab as a tool to help him get better sleep. When I completed the short questionnaire to get started, the feature didn't work but instead gave me a cheeky error message and has never worked despite repeated attempts.

4) My sister in law babysat for us and she has an older iPhone that had a different version of the Owlet App, we wanted her to be able to check in on baby so she downloaded it and we logged her in. She was able to use it successfully and we were able to check in on baby while we were out. After she left, we realized that somehow the camera had been disconnected from our account. We aren't sure if/how/why this would have been related to her using the account on the other version of the app but given the timing it feels like it can't be a coincidence. My husband then spent 45 minutes trying to get the camera to reconnect to the app on his Android phone and couldn't do it. I was able to reconnect the camera to the account on my iPhone app.

For the amount of money that we spent on this camera, frankly I expected more from the app. It's been increasingly frustrating the longer we've used it and in hindsight we both agree that if we had known then what we know now we would have opted to choose a different brand of camera for our son's nursery. For now we're sticking with it, but are exploring other options to purchase if we get disconnected again or continue to encounter new/different issues with the camera

Imagine - you hear a LOUD thump from your child's room. You KNOW if you go in there, the child will wake and won't sleep again for hours. But - not to worry! You've got the Owlet Cam Baby Monitor in your child's room and the app on your iPad. You open the app, looking to the screen for reassurance - and you see an AD. A SALES AD FOR MORE OF THEIR CRAP. Now, my son has seizures, so being able to assess him as quickly as possible is a MAJOR priority. I could have fumbled around, half asleep - attempting to close the ad so I can see my child, but I needed to check him ASAP and I didn't have time to mess with this BS, and I got up and ran to the room to check on him.

He was just fine - cats causing mayhem, that was all. And my son was delighted to see me at 3 am. We spent from 3 to 6 spending some quality time together. And in my sleep deprived state, I realized how invasive, how inconsiderate - how ridiculous it is for a baby camera company to knowingly display ads OVER the video content the parents bought the camera to see. It's revolting. But surely there's a way to shut OFF the ads, right? I contacted the company and they said I could get rid of the ads simply by clicking the the right hand corner whenever they appear. OML.

And - right now it's ads about their own products. But - there's no guarantee they won't open up this as a lucrative advertising market. I mean, captive audience - incredibly targeted. And the company clearly has no moral objections to crap like this.

To be fair - I did not ASK if the camera I was going to purchase would display ads on the app. I mean - the very idea of it is so objectionable and offensive, who would have thought? Thanks Owlet, you've taught me that whatever I've thought of company ethics up till now, well - it's a whole lot worse than I am capable of anticipating.

As a mom with anxiety who has already lost a baby, this is what I desperately needed and wanted when we were expecting our second little one. I needed to have the camera, the night vision, the audio, the heart rate, the breathing, all at my finger tips. So when I was shopping around and saw this, I thought this would be everything I ever dreamed of.
Let me assure you- it’s not. After a year of use, I am ready to throw this in the garbage and buy a new one.

Let me start by saying the sock is amazing. It did everything I wanted and needed. It is perfect. I will continue to use the sock even after replacing the camera. If you invest in anything from Owlet, let it be the sock and only the sock.

Now, for the camera. The absolute bane of my existence. This camera NNEEVVEERR stays connected. I will open the app after I have JUST put my little one to bed and what do you know, it says No Connection or Camera Offline. I restart the app, nothing. I log out of my account and back in, nothing. I restart my phone, nothing. I turn off the wifi on my phone and try it without wifi, nothing. I try turning my wifi back on, STILL nothing. At this point, my only choice is to go into my little ones bedroom, risk waking her up and unplugging the camera to restart it— or press and hold the button to reset it. When doing this, it will announce “RESETTING” very loudly. If that’s not enough, when it does come back on, the blue status light which is surprisingly super bright also comes back on and shines directly into my little ones face. Then, it announces very loudly “READY TO PAIR” while flashing a bright blue and red light. Then in the process of pairing to your phone, it has you hold a QR code from your phone up to the camera. When it does that, it makes your phone screen as bright as possible so the camera can read, also just to ensure it wakes your little one up with even MORE bright lights like the status light wasn’t enough. When it has successfully read the QR code, it makes an extremely loud chime noise to let you know it scanned successfully. If somehow you have gone through all that and your little one hasn’t woken up, guess what, SOMETIMES THAT FAILS AT THE VERY END AND YOU HAVE TO START OVER FROM SCRATCH AND DO EVERYTHING I MENTIONED ABOVE ALL OVER AGAIN. That happens probably 40-50% of the time.

So say by some miracle you have managed to reconnect the camera and baby is still asleep. THANK MERCIFUL GOD. You finally get the camera set up on your nightstand for you to see and settle down. Uh oh, you forgot to set your alarms for the morning. Or you get a notification, or you forget to turn the sound down slightly. So you switch apps, or simply just pull down and open the control center to turn the volume down. GUESS WHAT. YOU HAVE STRAYED FROM THE APP SO THE CAMERA DISCONNECTS AND HAS TO RELOAD WHEN YOU GO BACK TO THE APP. AND GUESS WHAT, SOMETIMES, IT WONT RELOAD. SO GUESS WHAT THAT MEANS? YOU HAVE TO GO BACK THROUGH THE LITERAL HELL I MENTIONED ABOVE.

It freezes. It lags. If at any point you want to have the camera up to monitor baby, you now have lost use of your phone. And if you have a power outage at any point, the camera does not reconnect to your internet or phone automatically. You have to go through the literal hell mentioned above. Or if you have to restart your router, you have to go through the literal hell mentioned above. Or if for some reason you try to disconnect the camera from the app and re-add the device to your account but the camera doesn’t get turned off or anything, you still have to go through the literal hell mentioned above.

Sometimes the camera works on my phone and tells my husband the camera is offline (when clearly it isn’t.) Sometimes it works for my husbands phone but tells me there is no connection (when clearly there is.)

- runs background audio (when it's not glitching out anyway) - which is amazing b/c you can be listening to a podcast or music and hear the feed

- allows multiple users to have access (some cheapie cams do not)

Neutral:
- good resolution (although no better than cheapie cams)

Cons:
- The glitchiness. You're just as likely to see a spinning wheel or blank screen as you are your sleeping child
- Not possible to simultaneously view two cameras, so if you have multiple children you can only hear/see one at a time
- No option to store, record, or review footage; live view only

- No freestanding monitor option and no ability to remove user access on app making this not ideal for babysitter situations

Overall I do no recommend this product at all. The glitchiness is maddening. Being up at 2 AM and seeing a spinning wheel instead of your baby is beyond frustrating. Defective right from the start - Eufy unwilling to help! AVOID!. We've experienced some glitches with the camera since unboxing it in June 2022. (Note we purchased it in Nov 2021, but actually didn't begin using it until June 2022, as we had our V-Tech single camera baby monitor set up in my 1 year old sons room, and had no need for dual cameras until we moved my newborn infant out of the bassinet in master bedroom into his own nursery).

Since the beginning of using it in June 2022, we have noticed some buggy behavior with the system. Which, at first, was never enough for us to want to give up using it, but definitely inconvenienced us frequently. We liked the features and video quality, so we were determined to make it work!

I did extensive research to choose a monitor system that fit our needs, and the VOX was one of the most important features for us (and remaining off wifi).

Since the start, the VOX has been hit/miss. Some days it works, some days it doesn't. My baby can be screaming in his crib, and the VOX doesn't detect his cries. Only me hearing it faintly through our ventilation system while I'm working was how I realized he was crying. I would then have to manually turn on the parent unit screen (pressing any button) to see my poor baby clearly in distress. The VOX was not registering his cries. Odd.

Every single time this happened, I would check the VOX settings and l would confirm that it is turned on, and set to be sensitive (so that even a burp should trigger the screen). Yet almost every time, it fails to work. This has been extremely frustrating...But, the hassle of returning a dual camera unit with a newborn and a 1 year old outweighed the issues at hand because I couldn't fathom not having a dual camera on hand - even if faulty. So I bit my tongue and ignored the persistent issue with VOX.

The second issue which plagues us is, and is almost more frustrating, is the unit constantly powers off overnight, while the unit is plugged in (receiving constant power, as noted by the red charging light), and the power of the unit itself was ON when I put it down on my nightstand. Again, I'd wake up to the sounds of my son crying, roll over and touch any button to illuminate the screen (since we know VOX isn't working), to find out, yet again, the power is off! This happens so frequently! I've checked the charging cable, outlet and port- all connections were fine. When I power the unit back on, it has full battery. So it's not a case where the battery has simply died overnight (and we keep it plugged in, so that it won't die over night). This has happened since unboxing it. Another odd behavior of the unit.

Another issue that has only gotten progressively worse is the connection of the cameras to the base/parent unit. If I'm out of range (say deep in the basement storage room), the parent unit will beep and notify me. Great- it's working as expected. But - if I'm sitting in the same spot in my living room, directly below my sons' bedrooms and the signal continues to drop (when it wasn't doing that before), it becomes an issue. Or in the middle of the night, when it is still powered on as it should be, it begins to beep randomly because of a lost signal.

My bedroom is right next to and right across from my sons' rooms. No thick walls, concrete or heavy metal obstructions. This issue is newer and quite annoying. I'm sure you can imagine how startling it can be when I'm woken from sleep because the monitor isn't connecting to a camera. Not being woken because one of my sons is awake, but rather the beeping from the monitor. When I roll over to check the boys rooms, the connection restores and they are asleep in bed. I constantly ensure the cameras are plugged in properly so that they too are receiving power - using the cables provided.

I've plugged them in to do software updates and none of these issues cease. There doesn't seem to be any fix.

Now, the newest issue that has (finally) pushed me to the point of enough frustration worthy to finally reach out to Eufy is now the charging port on the parent unit seems to have connection issues. This is new, as in we noticed it the last month or two.

The unit has not been dropped, smashed or in any way damaged. Yet the parent unit struggles to maintain a connection with the cable to charge. The red indicator light next to the charging port flickers as if the power current is being interrupted. You have to carefully get a connection and not touch it again or the light will turn off, stopping the unit from charging, and the battery begins to drain.

We have tested multiple charging cords on multiple outlets. It appears to be the female port on the unit itself that is faulty. This is making the unit difficult to charge. (And thus, now, may turn off overnight - completely unrelated to the original issue where the unit would power off unexpectedly as discussed before). Now the battery is draining and dying sometime overnight.

So, as you can see, the monitor we have seems to be plagued with issues. I reached out to Eufy, and since I purchased it JUST over a year ago (but only actually USING it less than a year) they will not refund or replace the unit. They agreed that we received a defective monitor, but won't replace it.

Additionally, because I ordered it from Amazon.com to be shipped to Canada, they said ALL warranty is VOID because it was shipped out of the USA. HUH? Seriously? Is their product that volatile that crossing the boarder into Canada renders their product useless and they won't back their products?

I spent $285 CAD on this unit. And all Eufy will do is offer a 15% off a product up to a MAX value of $100! Seriously?! Not even enough to cover actually replacing the unit itself. What a shame! I am so disappointed with Eufy and will not purchase their products again! AVOID the hassle!

So anyway, we asked if they could instead ship us out a monitor/camera set that is pre-paired to overcome this idiotic issue. No dice. Their solution? Go buy a PC, sorry, we can't help you further.

So now what? Stuck with an ugly paperweight? Amazon won't return the monitor since it is outside of their return window. What useless customer service and now useless product.

Again ------ beware if you actually care about security. Firmware updates are usually necessary to keep your cameras and devices up-to-date with the latest patches to prevent unauthorized access. If a company selling these devices can't figure out how to have these firmware updates installed, that should be a HUGE red flag.

And if you don't know, now you know
